limits: This is a review-fix correctness follow-up using numeric source inputs and real native Node worker/broker processes; baseline counterexamples were not rerun.
The new timeout/channel/finish bounds and CLI failure exits have focused regressions; the seven native broker cases are the existing integration smoke, not elapsed-time boundary fault injection.
The load-hook CLI regressions stub only the expensive workload in isolated child-process copies; their original cleanup/report/CLI status tails execute. They do not qualify a real broker.
Thirteen observed child workers include expected exit1 recoveries and two deliberate SIGKILL crashes; final replacements exit0 and no processes remain.
No full-chain SHIP decoding, live-fork recovery, Elasticsearch durability, master restart, host power loss, throughput or runtime capacity claim.
Dependencies were reused through a documented symlink to the existing pinned npm tree without reinstall or mutation. Source/build/native snapshots and the lock are retained.
The credential-duplication orchestration pilot is preserved and excluded; it failed before any cases, workers or queues. Existing qualification and baseline evidence remain unchanged.
Fixture credentials and producer key are public test-only data for the isolated disposable services.
